assumptions: Assumed that Oculus Browser and Oculus Desktop run on the same underlying host operating system.
Assumed that potentially executing code via Oculus Browser HTML injection produces an unprivileged operating system process rather than being restricted to a sandboxed browser environment.

evidence_quotes.quote: inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI

missing_conditions: Confirmation that Oculus Browser and Oculus Desktop are co-located on the same host platform.
Confirmation that the source vulnerability actually achieves local code execution beyond UI spoofing/HTML injection.
Verification that the resulting process context satisfies the unprivileged process requirements to receive or interact with handles from OVRServiceLauncher.exe.
response.reason: CVE-2019-3562 enables HTML injection into the Oculus Browser UI, which may 'potentially execute code'. CVE-2021-24038 requires 'an unprivileged process' to expose a privileged process handle from OVRServiceLauncher.exe for 'local privilege escalation'. The transition is conditional because code execution is only potential, browser sandboxing may prevent operating system-level process interaction, and same-host deployment of both components is unverified.
